SCIENTIFIC R PACKAGE · STABLE GITHUB RELEASE 0.4.3

From eye movements to mathematical trajectories.

Explore eye movements as time-varying mathematical trajectories. Use native R functional data analysis, kinematics, distances, recurrence and experimental statistical methods, with optional Python integration and explicit scientific limitations.

NEW · COMPLETE SCIENTIFIC METHODS ATLAS

904 exported interfaces. One transparent scientific evidence registry.

Search the entire published v0.4.3 API by intended scientific tier, execution backend and method-specific evidence status. The catalogue distinguishes 41 curated method records from explicitly provisional classifications; it never equates API breadth with independent validation.

Browse scientific methods →

NEW · FOUR EXECUTED R RESEARCH WORKFLOWS

Complete analyses from research question to reproducible figures.

Explore dense MFPCA, descriptive repeated-measures decomposition, sparse PACE recovery and participant-level bootstrap uncertainty. All four examples use synthetic data, generate real native R figures and state their inferential limits.

Explore four complete R studies →

NEW · RESEARCH WORKFLOW PORTAL

From CSV structure to the appropriate scientific R workflow.

Inspect a local eye-tracking CSV without uploading it, choose methods by observation grid, estimand and participant hierarchy, and explore ten exported native-R workflow routes alongside real figures, source references and scientific limitations. No browser-side model fitting or automatic inference claims.

Open Research Workflow Portal →

NEW · VERIFIED REAL-DATA PERFORMANCE BENCHMARK

Pairwise trajectory distances, 104–215× faster in the tested configurations.

On real OneStop fixation trajectories, the R-only weighted L² distance optimization reduced the 1,000-curve, 128-point median from 31.91 s to 0.305 s, with 21/21 declared numerical checks passing. Explore all six configurations, the numerical safeguards, and the release-version boundary. This is a development-branch benchmark, not a change to the archived v0.4.3 software.

Read the benchmark and limitations →

BEYOND VISUALIZATION

Three methods. Three ways to understand a trajectory.

A trajectory’s shape, timing, and return structure reveal different information. Explore what changes when you adjust the data—and where interpretation depends on modelling assumptions.

φ₁(t) 01 · FUNCTIONAL DATA ANALYSIS Functional PCA Decompose variation across whole curves and inspect reconstruction errors as more components are retained. Try the live example → DTW 02 · TEMPORAL ALIGNMENT Dynamic time warping Change the phase of two signals and trace the minimum-cost monotone alignment. Try the live example → Rᵢⱼ 03 · NONLINEAR DYNAMICS Recurrence analysis Change state-space radius and temporal exclusion, then inspect the recurrence matrix and line statistics. Try the live example →

Educational browser implementations with synthetic trajectories. For real analyses, use the documented R methods and inspect their assumptions. Compare all interactive laboratories.

TWO IMPLEMENTATION PATHS

Native R first. Python only when requested.

PATH A · PYTHON-FREE

Native R

Use native trajectory structures and functions for documented scientific methods without initializing Python.

Read the native R quick start →

PATH B · OPTIONAL

Python 1.2 bridge

Call selected published Python methods through reticulate. Python wrappers are not automatically equivalent to native R algorithms.

Understand the Python bridge →
